policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'then we knew' is first person plural, matching ἐπέγνωμεν; ἐπέγνωσαν would give 'they knew'.
ASV text reads 'Melita' (Μελίτη); its mapped textual note relegates 'Melitene' (Μελιτήνη) to the margin as a reading of some authorities.
τε and δέ are both carried by ASV's opening 'And'; no wording in the verse distinguishes the connective and no note is mapped here.
ἅψαντες and ἀνάψαντες both yield 'they kindled a fire'; the compound prefix leaves no trace in the ASV.

English requires an article before 'a bundle of sticks' whether or not τι stands with πλῆθος, so presence or omission is not distinguished. The verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.
ἀπό and ἐκ are both rendered 'by reason of the heat' (margin 'from the heat'); that note is an alternative_rendering about English wording and decides nothing.
ASV 'a viper came out' fits ἐξελθοῦσα and equally the compound διεξελθοῦσα, whose δια- is not separately represented.
A transposition of ἔλεγον and πρὸς ἀλλήλους; English word order in 'they said one to another' is fixed by its own grammar.
Aorist μεταβαλόμενοι and present μεταβαλλόμενοι alike give 'they changed their minds'; the aspect is not marked in the ASV.
Word order only within the infinitive clause; 'that he was a god' renders either arrangement.
Transposition of τρεῖς and ἡμέρας; ASV 'three days' is the only possible English either way.
δυσεντερίῳ and δυσεντερίᾳ differ only in declension of the same noun; both are 'dysentery'.
ASV's 'And when this was done' is its default connective and covers both δέ and οὖν; nothing else in the verse marks an inferential force.
Transposition of ἐν τῇ νήσῳ around the participle; 'that had diseases in the island' renders either order.
πρὸς τὰς χρείας and πρὸς τὴν χρείαν are both carried by the idiomatic 'such things as we needed', which supplies 'things' from the sense rather than from the number of χρεία.
ASV 'we set sail' renders ἀνάγω of putting to sea; bare ἤχθημεν would be 'we were brought/led' and gives no nautical sense.
ASV text 'we made a circuit' renders περιελθόντες (περιέρχομαι); the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read cast loose' puts περιελόντες in the margin.
παρ' αὐτοῖς and ἐπ' αὐτοῖς are both rendered 'with them'.
ASV 'came to meet us' has no 'out'; ASV represents ἐξέρχομαι with 'went/came out', so the simple ἦλθαν is what stands here.
ASV 'when we entered into Rome' renders the compound εἰσήλθομεν; bare ἤλθομεν would be 'we came to Rome'.
ASV text goes straight from entering Rome to 'Paul was suffered to abide', and its mapped textual note places the centurion clause in the margin as an insertion of some authorities.
ASV 'he called together' uses a pronoun; τὸν Παῦλον would have named Paul, as the verse names him nowhere.

ASV 'I, brethren, though I had done nothing' places the pronoun first, which excludes the RP order Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἐγώ (r02); the remaining two readings differ only in editorial punctuation, which the ASV does not settle.
Present κατηγορεῖν and aorist κατηγορῆσαι are both 'to accuse'; the ASV infinitive marks no aspect.
Transposition of ἡμῖν and ἐστιν; 'it is known to us' renders either order.
ἧκον and ἦλθον are both rendered 'they came'.
ASV 'persuading them concerning Jesus' has the accusative pronoun as sole object; the added τά would give 'the things concerning Jesus', which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'unto your fathers' is second person, matching ὑμῶν against ἡμῶν ('our fathers').
λέγων and λέγον differ only in the gender agreement of the participle; both are ASV's 'saying'.
Transposition of ἔστω and ὑμῖν; 'Be it known therefore unto you' renders either order. The verse's mapped note concerns the insertion of verse 29, not this unit.
ASV 'this salvation of God' represents τοῦτο; the RP omission leaves no demonstrative to render.
The ASV text ends the verse at 'they will also hear', and its mapped textual note places verse 29 in the margin as an insertion of some authorities.
Ἐνέμεινεν and ἔμεινεν are both rendered 'he abode'; the ἐν- prefix is not separately represented.
ASV 'And he abode' uses a pronoun subject; the added ὁ Παῦλος would have named Paul here.
